stem.en: Kula, grāma, viśha and jana fitted together in Vedic society. Which statement best describes this arrangement?

text.en: Each group gave orders to the one below it, so a village had no say and the rājā decided everything.
The four groups replaced one another over time, so the kula had disappeared once the jana formed.
The rājā served as chief protector of the jana, and the family was inseparable from the people.
The rājā made laws for every group, and each group existed only to carry out his orders.

explanation.en: The sources call the rājā the chief protector of the jana. A family sat inside a village, a village inside a viśha and a viśha inside the jana, so the kula was inseparable from the people. Options a and d describe a chain of command, which these sources do not describe. Option b is wrong because all four groups existed together.

hints.en: Which word do the sources use for the rājā's role: protector or lawmaker?
Did a family stop existing when a jana formed?
